raw_response:
I would trial **HESK in knowledgebase-only mode** first. It is the closest documented match I found for your requested content, Windows deployment, and free licensing. This is a documentation-based recommendation; I have not installed it or measured whether it is faster than your phpMyFAQ installation.

### 1. HESK — strongest fit

The [self-hosted download](https://www.hesk.com/download.php) is free and uses PHP/MySQL. Its [server requirements](https://www.hesk.com/knowledgebase/index.php?article=32) explicitly include Windows. The current download page identifies version 3.7.13, released on 18 October 2026, and lists supported PHP/MySQL versions.

Your heading, body, category, and attachment requirements are demonstrated together in the vendor's [public example article](https://www.hesk.com/demo/knowledgebase.php?article=3). The [dated changelog](https://www.hesk.com/help/docs/changelog.html) records article keywords and a knowledgebase-only mode. That mode is particularly relevant because you do not want an unnecessarily broad application interface.

Configure public knowledgebase categories and leave whole-site mandatory customer authentication disabled. The [quick-start guide](https://www.hesk.com/knowledgebase/?article=109) distinguishes public knowledgebase access from the option that hides the entire help desk behind login. It also places knowledgebase management in the authenticated administration area, with staff permissions.

The practical caveats are that the underlying product is still a help desk, its performance with your data is unmeasured, and I did not verify SSO. Before committing, try representative articles, keyword searches, and your actual attachment types on your Windows/PHP/MySQL configuration. The documentation supports the requested setup; it does not establish that your existing bugs or latency will disappear.

### 2. PHPKB — commercial alternative with unresolved price/edition details

[PHPKB](https://www.phpkb.com/) is another relevant self-hosted candidate. Its [requirements](https://www.phpkb.com/requirements) explicitly cover Windows, Apache/IIS, PHP, and MySQL. The [feature list](https://www.phpkb.com/features-list) documents article editing, hierarchical categories, attachments, search, and controlled authoring. Its [unrestricted access mode](https://www.phpkb.com/features/access-modes) allows guests to read public categories.

The same feature list advertises self-hosted pricing from USD 285, and its [licensing page](https://www.phpkb.com/pricing) describes perpetual licenses. Whether that is a low cost for your project is unresolved, and the dynamically configured checkout did not provide a final selected-edition quote. Article Keywords appears in the feature navigation, but I did not verify its precise behavior or inclusion in the edition you would buy. SSO options are advertised; confirm their edition and add-on costs.

I would keep PHPKB on the shortlist only pending those checks. Its broad feature set also makes it less obviously aligned with your desire for simplicity.

### 3. DokuWiki — unverified alternative approach

A wiki-based FAQ might be worth investigating, so I also considered [DokuWiki](https://www.dokuwiki.org/dokuwiki). Its official documentation was inaccessible in this research run, and the accessible [official repository](https://github.com/dokuwiki/dokuwiki) excerpt did not establish the required configuration. I therefore cannot confirm the content fields, access controls, Windows setup, or any required plugins from the evidence I obtained. This is a follow-up lead, not a verified replacement.

The clearest next step is a small HESK knowledgebase-only trial. PHP/MySQL are preferences in your question, and SSO is a bonus; neither should override the required article content, anonymous reading, authenticated editing, Windows support, and acceptable acquisition cost. Most sources are live and undated, so the explicitly dated HESK releases provide stronger timing evidence than the current commercial feature pages.
